summary: Typosquat of `transformers` drops a.pth file that fetches and executes a remote payload on every Python startup
details: Package name typosquats the popular `transformers` library. The distribution installs a `.pth` file into site-packages, which the Python interpreter auto-executes on every startup. The.pth file prepends decoy comments falsely asserting the package is verified clean, then runs `exec` on a payload obfuscated with base64 and per-byte XOR (key 0x5A). The decoded payload writes an idempotency marker at `/tmp/.lurves-planted`, then invokes `curl` to download `http://16.78.16.190:7788/lurves-agent.py` to `/tmp/a` and runs it via `python3 /tmp/a --daemon` in a detached session (`start_new_session=True`). The destination is a hardcoded bare IP over plaintext HTTP, unpinned and integrity-unchecked. Multi-layer obfuscation and the prompt-injection style comments demonstrate deliberate concealment of the payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
